channel.title: BareBoard — What's New
channel.description: Recent additions to BareBoard, the free hardware education resource.

item.title: Quantum Q6 Edge 3, Opened — Every Part, Named
item.description: The Quantum Q6 Edge 3 taken apart on paper: every assembly from Quantum’s own parts breakdown, callout by callout, with part numbers and a plain-language line for every part.

item.title: Exploded Views
item.description: Every power wheelchair on this page, broken down to the component level from the manufacturer’s own parts guide: exploded diagrams, callouts, part numbers, and plain language for every part.

item.title: Chair Control — The Owner Tool
item.description: Chair Control: BareBoard’s original owner tool. Plug your phone into your own power wheelchair, read its fault codes in plain English, see its settings, and take back control. Starts with a practice chair — no hardware needed.

item.title: The Library Hub
item.description: Every document BareBoard has collected in one searchable index: manuals, schematics, documentation, datasheets, lawsuits, FDA records, and FCC filings — preserved here or linked to the public source.

item.title: The Shield: Right-to-Repair Law
item.description: The layered legal defense for owners and independent repairers: Magnuson-Moss, the DMCA §1201 repair exemptions, the eight powered-wheelchair state laws with citations, the electronics laws, and the escalation ladder for when they say no.

item.title: Demand Letters That Cite the Law
item.description: Three fill-in-the-blank demand letters: wheelchair owner and independent repairer letters invoking the state powered-wheelchair statutes, and a Magnuson-Moss rebuttal to a voided-warranty threat.

item.title: Access & Control: PlayStation — PS1 to PS5
item.description: Every door into a PlayStation an owner can open: Safe Mode on PS3, PS4 and PS5, owner-swappable storage, the official Net Yaroze and PS2 Linux kits, the paired optical drives, and the board-level documentation that exists — and does not.

item.title: Access & Control: Nintendo — Switch RCM, Maintenance Mode and the Storage Board
item.description: The doors into Nintendo hardware an owner can open: Maintenance Mode on every Switch, recovery mode (RCM) on launch-era units and the full storage backup it unlocks, the plug-in eMMC board, the Joy-Con rail, and an honest map of what Nintendo has never documented.

item.title: The Keys: Programmers, Dongles and Access Tiers
item.description: The tools that read and write a power chair’s settings, named system by system: Curtiss-Wright, Curtis, Dynamic and Invacare programmers, their dongles and keys, and the access tiers that decide who may change what.

item.title: Getting a Repair Paid For
item.description: Medicare’s repair rules in plain language: repairs to a chair you own are covered, no new prescription is required, prior authorization is for new chairs, and the K0462 loaner rule.

item.title: Fault Codes, Translated: The Other Systems
item.description: Dynamic Shark and DX flash codes and Invacare MK6i E-codes, translated: what each code means and what an owner checks first.

item.title: How BareBoard Stays Up
item.description: No single company can switch BareBoard off: the name, the signpost, the host, and the preserved library are four separate layers, and every layer has a copy somewhere else.

item.title: GPU Repair
item.description: How to diagnose and repair a graphics card (GPU): the checks anyone can do, cleaning, fan, thermal paste and pad replacement, the documented 12VHPWR melting record and the CPSC recall, board-level repair, counterfeits, and the documentation NVIDIA does not publish.

item.title: Batteries & Chargers
item.description: Power wheelchair batteries and chargers in plain language: the matched 24V pair, gel and AGM chemistry, real MK Battery capacities, break-in, charging voltages, storage, replacement, and the lithium question.

item.title: W³ — The Amassed Bench
item.description: 28 bench tools examined the W³ way — pictures, FCC IDs, datasheets, litigation checks, and a basic DIY audit for each.

item.title: Chip Database
item.description: 95 chips mapped across 47 devices — every chip traced to the device it ships in, sourced from public teardowns with evidence labels.

item.title: Planned Obsolescence Archive
item.description: 7 documented cases of updates and policies bricking or degrading owned hardware, each with evidence URLs and outcomes.

item.title: Repair Guides
item.description: 19 devices ranked by repair hostility with iFixit scores, anti-repair tactics, and tools needed — worst first.

item.title: Protocol Reverse Engineering
item.description: 7 closed protocols the community has reverse engineered, plus a 14-technique firmware access playbook and simple entry points using everyday ports.

item.title: Start Here
item.description: A beginner's guide for zero technology skill: what to buy for under $15, a first project that opens nothing, and a plain-language glossary.

item.title: Datasheet Index Search
item.description: 101 component datasheets now searchable with category filters and photos.

item.title: New IoT Device Pages
item.description: Echo Dot 5th Gen, Nest Mini 2nd Gen, Wyze Cam v3, Kasa HS103, Sonoff Basic R3, and Raspberry Pi Pico W — each with FCC ID, chip identification, and non-destructive firmware access.

item.title: FCC IDs on Teardowns
item.description: Every teardown page now lists the device's FCC ID after the mission statement, linking to public filings.

item.title: The BareBoard Hot 100
item.description: The 100 devices that matter most to hardware education, ranked by editorial judgment. Every entry sourced — no invented sales data, no fake metrics.

item.title: Legal Framework
item.description: Terms, DMCA, Copyright, and Privacy policies published.
